key_insight: ISLA builds physical invariances into a transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs, making predictions robust to coordinate changes, declared units, and boundary mesh refinement.
engineering_relevance: This approach could make aerodynamic surrogates more reliable across object poses, scales, and meshes without retraining for each representation.
method: Uses distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors; no learned operation receives coordinates.
Weights boundary sums by quadrature and normalizes lengths using a boundary-derived unit.
Predicts interior fields through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel, with each query independent of other queries.
evidence_signal: On AeroZoo's 2,816 flows, mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors are at least 3.1× and 3.3× lower than any baseline's; on AirfRANS, ISLA ranks behind GLOBE but beats Transolver and GeoTransolver by at least 1.6×.
watch_item: The abstract evaluates steady, boundary-driven flows; applicability to unsteady turbulence and the cost of exact boundary reads remain to be assessed.
paper_title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
